title: Localizable bottom-up household load model
description:
A localizable, decomposable bottom-up model of residential electricity demand with resolution down to one second. Probabilistic occupancy (a Markov chain driven by a time-use survey) switches appliances with measured power traces, and the seasonal shape is localized by the national standard load profile, so no local time-use survey is required. Demand can be decomposed down to the individual appliance, which enables efficiency scenarios. Reactive power is modelled as a single constant capacitive parameter per connection point. Includes a PySide6 desktop application and an optional pvlib/PVGIS photovoltaic chain.

This is the reference implementation for the manuscript "A localisable bottom-up model of household load profiles with appliance-level decomposition: validation against five independent measurement sources" (Applied Energy).

Restricted validation data (distribution feeder and smart-meter measurements from the distribution system operators) are not included and are not required to run the model.
